title: Decide whether verify_smtp_signer (PKIX-fmtv.13) also gets DANE-default-on
description:
## What

PKIX-fmtv.13 introduces `verify_code_signer` + `verify_time_stamper` + `verify_ocsp_responder` thin wrappers. None of those are DANE-relevant. But there's a parallel question for the eventual SMTP DANE wrapper (RFC 7672) — is there a verify_smtp_dane / verify_smtp_signer / similar that also takes DANE-default-on?

## Why this matters

RFC 7672 SMTP-DANE has the strongest production deployment of any DANE flavor. MTAs negotiating TLS routinely use SMTP-DANE for trust. A workspace adopting DANE-default for HTTPS but not SMTP would be incomplete.

## Options

- **A) Yes, verify_smtp_signer / verify_smtp_dane gains DANE-default-on under same Cargo feature.** SMTP and HTTPS share the resolver + DANE primitives; only the wrapper differs (RFC 7672 SMTP-DANE has slightly different semantics — opportunistic, MX-name-derived TLSA query).

- **B) No, SMTP stays a separate decision.** Maybe in pkix-chain, maybe in a sibling pkix-smtp crate.

- **C) Defer.** Decide when verify_smtp_signer is actually being designed.

## Considerations

- 'Encourage DANE to spread' applies equally (or more) to SMTP.
- SMTP-DANE has known operational subtleties (MX records, DNSSEC down the chain, RFC 7672 §3 query construction) that may warrant its own wrapper / crate.

## Decision-gate

Human-labeled. Probably resolves when verify_smtp_signer work begins.
close_reason:
CLOSED 2026-11-24 (Mark, interactive) as mis-framed. Real SMTP-DANE work filed separately.

## Why the question cannot be answered as posed

The bead asks whether 'verify_smtp_signer (PKIX-fmtv.13)' should get DANE-default-on. Two problems:

1. verify_smtp_signer does not exist and was never designed. PKIX-fmtv.13 delivered verify_code_signer, verify_time_stamper and verify_ocsp_responder; the bead itself notes none of those is DANE-relevant, then speculates about 'verify_smtp_dane / verify_smtp_signer / similar'.
2. SMTP-DANE is not a signer verification. RFC 7672 governs the TLS certificate of a mail server an MTA connects to — a TLS SERVER check. The workspace's verify_smime_signer / verify_smime_recipient are S/MIME message signing, an unrelated concern that merely shares the word 'mail'. A '_signer' entry point is the wrong home for SMTP-DANE regardless of the DANE-default answer.

## What replaces it

The bead's own instinct — 'may warrant its own wrapper / crate' — is correct, and there is now a concrete reason beyond operational subtlety: a shared code path with verify_tls_server would be actively WRONG, not merely incomplete.

RFC 7672 differs from HTTPS-DANE behaviourally:

- Usage filtering. SMTP clients are, to the best of current understanding, required to ignore PKIX-TA(0) and PKIX-EE(1) records entirely, since public CA trust is not meaningful between MTAs that have no user to see a warning. If so, reusing verify_tls_server's DANE path would honour records RFC 7672 requires be ignored. NOT YET CONFIRMED against the RFC text — it is the first thing the implementing bead must check, and it is the reason a shared path is unsafe rather than just untidy.
- DNSSEC-validated MX lookup. The TLSA owner name derives from an MX lookup that must ITSELF be validated; an unvalidated MX lookup lets an attacker rewrite the MX and point at a server whose TLSA record they also control. This is a resolver-level requirement reaching into PKIX-j32w.2, not something a thin wrapper can add.
- Reference identity. Which name the certificate must match follows RFC 7672's MX-derived rules rather than RFC 6125's.

The epic's observation that SMTP-DANE has the strongest production deployment of any DANE flavour stands and is carried into the new bead, so the commitment is preserved without pretending a design exists.

## Option B of this bead, chosen in effect

'SMTP stays a separate decision; maybe in pkix-chain, maybe in a sibling crate' — with the placement question left to the new bead now that there is a reason to expect a separate entry point.
